content.thinking:
Random predicates give few rules. Real workloads probably similar. But let me construct a targeted adversarial case to check the throughput when rules number in the thousands. Design: make training truth masks be complements of small sets so that many minimal hitting sets exist, AND ensure falsifiers exist in the universe.

Setup: one field x with domain [0..63] plus one field y domain [0..1023] to make universe 65536? Universe doesn't need to be huge for rule-count stress. Let me use: field x domain [0..31], K=1, universe 32. Predicates p_i: x != i for i in 0..31? Then masks: row x=a → mask = all except a. Minimal hitting sets = pairs {i,j}, i≠j: C(32,2) = 496 rules. cond3: falsifier of {i,j}: x==i and x==j → impossible → all excluded. Damn.

Swap: predicates p_i: x == i? Row a mask = {a}: minimal hitting sets = sets containing all present... clause must contain bit for each mask... clause hits {a} iff a ∈ clause. All masks present → clause must contain all 32 → size> width.0 rules.

Use two fields x,y domain [0..15] (universe 256): predicates: p_i: x != i (i 0..15) and q_j: y != j (j 0..15) — 32 preds. Row (a,b): mask missing {p_a, q_b}. Minimal hitting sets: H hits mask(a,b) iff H \ {p_a,q_b} ≠ ∅. Minimal hitting sets: triples {p_i,q_j,r} where r ∉ ... any H with ≥3 elements hits all ✓ minimal as shown before (every pair fails). So minimal hitting sets = all 3-subsets that hit everything = all 3-subsets (any 3-subset: for any (a,b), |H\{p_a,q_b}| ≥ 1 ✓). Minimality: every pair fails (pair {u,v} fails mask where {a,b} = the pair's... pair {p_i,q_j} fails (i,j); pair {p_i,p_k} fails row (i,b) where mask missing {p_i,q_b}: H\{p_i,q_b} = {p_k} ≠ ∅ → hits! Hmm wait pair {p_i,p_k}: mask(a,b) missing {p_a,q_b}: H \ {p_a,q_b} = {p_i,p_k} minus {p_a} (q not in H) → if a==i: {p_k} nonempty ✓ hit; if a==k: {p_i} ✓; if a∉{i,k}: both ✓. So pair {p_i,p_k} hits ALL masks! Is it minimal? Remove p_i → {p_k}: fails mask (k,b) (any b): mask missing {p_k,q_b}: {p_k}\{p_k,q_b}=∅ → miss ✓ so p_i essential ✓. So all pairs of same-column preds are minimal hitting sets! {p_i,p_k}: 16×15/2 = 120 pairs; similarly q-pairs 120; mixed pairs {p_i,q_j} fail (row (i,j)). Triples: all hit; minimal iff no pair sub-clause hits: mixed triples {p_i,q_j,r}: pairs {p_i,r}... if r = p_k: pair {p_i,p_k} hits all → triple non-minimal. Mixed triple with 2 q's + 1 p: {p_i,q_j,q_k}: pair {q_j,q_k} hits → non-minimal. So minimal = all same-column pairs = 240 rules. Plus size-1? {p_i}: fails mask (i,b) → not hitting. Total 240 rules. cond3: falsify pair {p_i,p_k}: x==i ∧ x==k → impossible → tautology!! All excluded! Argh — same-column ne preds are never jointly false.

The universe constraint says: for a clause of ne-on-same-cell predicates to have a counterexample... Any clause whose literals cannot be simultaneously false is a tautology and excluded. So high rule counts require predicates with overlapping falsifier sets. This inherently limits rule counts... but not necessarily to small numbers: e.g., predicates with LARGE falsifying sets and random-ish truth masks.

Example: x domain [0..9], y domain [0..6553] (U=65536). 32 predicates: p_i: x == i for i in 0..9 (10 preds), plus predicates q: x >= 3 etc. Hmm.

Alternative: K=4, one field x domain [0..3] (U = 256) and predicates over sums/scales: each predicate has arbitrary falsifying subset of the 256 windows (a comparison divides windows). With 32 random comparisons over 4 cells, masks are random-ish half-sets over 256 windows and rows. Minimal hitting sets of random 50/50 masks over 32 elements: minimal hitting sets are mostly singletons/pairs... With N training rows large, family of random masks = almost all possible masks → minimal hitting sets = singletons where bit always true... For random full-support families: minimal hitting sets of the family of ALL masks = ∅ (empty mask in family → impossible; empty mask occurs if some row has all-false). If family = all nonempty masks: minimal hitting sets = singletons! (every singleton hits all nonempty masks ✓ and each is minimal ✓) → 32 rules if each singleton has privates... priv of {i}: rows where only i true — exists for each i with enough rows. cond3: falsify {i}: window with p_i false ✓. So ~32 rules.

For pairs to be rules: need pairs minimal: each i needs private row where only i among {i,j} true. Random masks over training rows with 32 preds: expected ~32 + pairs... Given random masks, minimal hitting sets of size k exist when... H hits all masks iff no mask⊆ complement... With N random masks, a pair {i,j} hits all masks iff no mask avoids both i,j: prob per mask avoid both = 2^-2 → with N=10000 rows none? 10000 × 1/4 — no. So pairs don't hit.

To get many rules: few training masks (family small), large masks. E.g., N small: 10 rows with random half-true masks: minimal hitting sets of a10-mask family over 32 elements, size ≤ 4: could be numerous: each mask ~16 bits; hitting sets are... transversals of 10 sets of size 16 in universe of 32 → lots of small transversals! E.g., C(32,2)=496 pairs, each pair hits a 16-bit mask w.p. 1-1/4=3/4; all 10: (3/4)^10 ≈ 5.6% → ~28 pairs; plus singles ~32×(1/2)^10 ≈ 0; triples: C(32,3)=4960 × (7/8)^10 ≈ 27% → ~1300 triples hit; minimal among them maybe several hundred... So with N=10 random 16-bit masks, maybe ~500-1500 rules of size ≤4. And cond3 requires falsifier windows in universe: random comparisons on universe of 256 windows: falsifier of H exists iff some window falsifies all literals (mask complement contains a universe mask...). Universe has256 windows → 256 masks over preds — a subset relation problem; likely fine.

Rule counts in the low thousands are plausible worst cases. JSON output for 5000 rules ≈ 500KB — trivial. Compute for rules: 5000 × priv+ce ≈ negligible.

I think performance is a non-issue now: measured end-to-end worst 1.4s for two max-size jobs. Let me nonetheless run a quick hunt with small N to see rule counts and timing (rulehunt with ntrain=10).

Also I want to fuzz with small train sizes and check duplicates in train (duplicates count as separate records — witness smallest index). My fuzz generator can produce duplicate rows naturally (rng.choice). OK.

One more edge to test: width > P; approved with clauses of length ≤ width but IDs valid; approved duplicates impossible; prefix strings like "01", "000", "9999999", "1000000"; target value 0 spelling "0". Let me add edge-case fuzz tweaks: prefixes from a broader set including "0", "00", "01", "1000000", "99999", "0000000". And domains including 0 and 1000000. Also K=4, nf=8 (cells=16). Let me extend the fuzz generator's ranges a bit and run more.

Also test multi-job with P=0 predicates and empty approved and empty queries. My generator allows P=0 and 0 queries ✓.

Let me run rulehunt with ntrain=10 variant and extended fuzz.

content.text: Random workloads yield few rules. Let me probe the plausible adversarial regime (tiny training sets → many minimal transversals) and extend fuzz edge coverage:

arguments.command: cd /workspace/dev && sed -i 's/def gen(rng, P=32, width=4, K=2, ntrain=200, dsize=8):/def gen(rng, P=32, width=4, K=2, ntrain=10, dsize=8):/' rulehunt.py && timeout 170 python3 rulehunt.py 11 300

cd /workspace/dev && python3 - <<'EOF'
s=open('fuzz.py').read()
# broader domains incl 0 and 1000000, broader prefixes
s=s.replace("domain = sorted(rng.sample(range(0, 12), size))",
"pool=[0,1,2,3,5,9,10,11,1000000]+list(range(4,9));domain = sorted(rng.sample(pool, size))")
s=s.replace("prefix = rng.choice(['', '0', '1', '10', '01', '3', '7777777', '12'])",
"prefix = rng.choice(['', '0', '00', '01', '1', '10', '3', '7777777', '12', '1000000', '99999', '0000000', '5'])")
s=s.replace("value = rng.randint(0, 15)","value = rng.choice([0,1,2,3,10,15,1000000])")
s=s.replace("return {'const': rng.randint(0, 15), 'type': rng.choice(['time','size','count','id','flag'])}",
"return {'const': rng.choice([0,1,2,3,10,15,1000000]), 'type': rng.choice(['time','size','count','id','flag'])}")
s=s.replace("'value': rng.randint(0, 15)}","'value': rng.choice([0,1,2,3,10,15,1000000])}")
s=s.replace("K = rng.randint(1, 3)","K = rng.randint(1, 4)")
s=s.replace("nf = rng.randint(1, 3)","nf = rng.randint(1, 3)")
s=s.replace("'scale': rng.randint(0, 20)","'scale': rng.choice([0,1,2,20,65535])")
open('fuzz.py','w').write(s)
EOF
timeout 170 python3 fuzz.py 5 400
